opening: Artificial Impossibility explores useful projects that cannot find anyone willing to support them.
Potential sponsors can follow reasonable rules while leaving the whole benefit unsupported.
The book maps those refusals without treating every barrier as a conspiracy.
Some obstacles protect rights, so moving a boundary also requires judgment.
Others arise when local mandates leave nobody responsible for the whole benefit.
Its distinctive move is to compare projects through their selection environments.
That gives readers a way to question what we too quickly call unrealistic.
books.spine: WHY: technically plausible value remains unsponsored. HOW: reconstruct the valuable outcome, identify mandates, test a different institutional arrangement. WHAT: three connected samples—anti-consumption agent, proof trap, public commons—show recurring patterns; smoothing conceals them; preserve protective boundaries; invite reading introduction and selected pattern chapters.
books.art: Amber architectural section theatre: a continuous project route meets three independently operated physical gates; each scene inspects one gate mechanism, then a plausible alternate route. No random labelled blocks. The barrier is a recurring source metaphor with visibly different mandate mechanisms.

opening: Enough for Everyone asks whether material security could become universal without limitless consumption.
It separates the resources Earth contains from services people can actually access.
The book’s answer is conditional optimism, grounded in infrastructure and institutional choices.
More available energy does not automatically produce a secure home or public freedom.
Its argument follows that gap through materials, food, robotics, ownership, and remaining scarcity.
The essential distinction is between providing enough and satisfying every possible desire.
Reading it means testing a practical threshold, rather than waiting for a technological miracle.
books.spine: WHY: ask a precise version of post-scarcity instead of infinite abundance. HOW: distinguish physical potential, built capacity, and access; trace one home’s services through energy, material and robotic bottlenecks. WHAT: ownership makes potential reach people; time, ecology and consent remain limited; scenario dates are conditional; read verdict and inspect its demonstration.
books.art: Warm terracotta and sea-blue civic cutaway: one elegant house gradually acquires actual services through power, water, repair and access. Scale changes between home, supply connection and shared neighborhood. No invented quantitative charts or endless growth imagery.

opening: Life Without an Audience asks who gets to author your inner life.
It begins with the imagined judgments we carry into ordinary decisions.
The book asks when other people’s reactions start making those decisions for us.
Its imagined teacher must eventually return that authority and become unnecessary.
Through psychology, old traditions, and AI, the lessons distinguish connection from capture.
The destination is not isolation or a perfectly self-sufficient personality.
It is a life answerable to others without being owned by their reactions.
books.spine: WHY: socially formed does not mean socially owned. HOW: the teacher leads an apprenticeship through internalized audience, metricized self, community capture, old practices and synthetic audience. WHAT: inner constitution distributes judgment among evidence, consequence, conscience and relationship; practical experiments remain nonclinical; the ending returns authority and invites the prologue.
books.art: Quiet aubergine and rose chamber theatre with a consistent expressive adult; a detached audience lens and small reaction counters recede while a real second person approaches. Empty chair, mirror and open doorway form source-specific continuity. No podium-guru worship or solitary triumph.

opening: Money Was Never One Thing reveals the hidden plurality inside an ordinary wallet.
A bank balance, airline points, and community credit do not carry identical promises.
The book uses that difference to reveal money as institutional design.
Its essential question is who writes the rules governing claims on future resources.
History, local experiments, and programmable money become ways to compare those rules.
The destination is neither one perfect currency nor an endorsement of every alternative.
Readers learn to inspect monetary governance before deciding which new design deserves trust.
books.spine: WHY: apparent single money hides distinct claims and governing powers. HOW: monetary design grammar compares issuer, acceptance, convertibility, loss and exit; mutual credit is a substantive example. WHAT: crypto moves trust, interoperability spreads opportunity and failure, AI might manage plural claims, constitutional questions remain; read prologue and design grammar before future scenarios.
books.art: Burgundy and teal numismatic editorial: a physical wallet unfolds into deliberately distinct claim instruments (bank slip, points pass, mutual-credit tally). Rotating views emphasize signatures, permissions and crossing an exchange threshold. Currency forms retain their differences across scenes; no market charts or price claims.

opening: The Captured Internet asks why a functioning network can become less worth entering.
Messages arrive while the rules governing attention escape the people living under them.
The book traces how useful platforms acquired power over identity, memory, and relevance.
Its proposed direction is governable networks with meaningful rights of voice and exit.
That requires institutions above open protocols, rather than nostalgia for an innocent early web.
The argument connects community governance, personal recommendation, and the architecture of communication.
Reading it means asking who can change the rules of your digital life.
books.spine: WHY: technical function can coexist with civic capture. HOW: history explains useful concentration; follow one community’s identity/relationships/archive into platform ownership. WHAT: distinguish licenses/constitution/provider contract; personal AI transfers policy control but risks echo/capture; trust-gated communication retains limits; read compressed opening then governance/recommender details.
books.art: Cobalt and coral network atlas: a community’s persistent address and archive travel from a central provider to plural hosts; routing, a visible recommendation dial and bounded introduction gate become narrative objects. Distinct topology changes carry the argument; no decorative mesh wallpaper.

opening: The Founder Lottery examines the hidden costs behind celebrated stories of entrepreneurial success.
Its winners can be real while the story told about typical outcomes remains misleading.
The book argues that AI may accelerate this race without correcting its rules.
Its constructive direction is to build shared institutions, not simply faster private companies.
Founders can preserve ambition while reusing trust, standards, and the memory of contribution.
Decentralized brands are the proposed architecture, with their risks and obligations left visible.
Reading it means reconsidering the game you build, rather than merely improving your next pitch.
books.spine: WHY: survivor mythology obscures distributed costs and typical founder experience. HOW: statistical distinction → AI Red Queen race → psychological near-miss and attention pressure → collaboration needs enforceable mechanics. WHAT: shared name as governed trust, contribution memory and fork/exit; begin with narrow comparative cohort; not every firm should decentralize; read preface and post-founder doctrine.
books.art: Deep blue and vermilion workshop theatre: one builder starts on a repeating audition track, then the stage opens into a cooperative workbench with shared tools and a common name. An explicit gate spotlight contrasts upper-tail winner with overlooked builders; no fake histogram or roulette literalism.
